header.running_head: Leading the Salaah and Following the Imaam During the Time of Rasulullaah ﷺ

blocks.text: Hadhrat Miswar (RA) pulls back an Imaam Whose Recitation was not Clear and Hadhrat Umar (RA) Sanctions his Act

Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) narrates that it was during the Hajj season when a large gathering of people amassed around a spring in Makkah. When the time for salaah arrived, a person who was not Arabic speaking and who belonged to the family of Hadhrat Abu Saa'ib Makhzoomi (RA) stepped forward (to lead the salaah). Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) pulled the man back and put another man forward. When the news reached Hadhrat Umar (RA), he said nothing to Hadhrat Miswar (RA) until Hadhrat Miswar (RA) arrived in Madinah. It was only when Hadhrat Miswar (RA) came to Madinah that Hadhrat Umar (RA) questioned him about it. "Give me a chance, O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" Hadhrat Miswar (RA) entreated. He then explained, "The man was not Arabic-speaking (whose recitation was unclear) and because it was during Hajj, I feared that some people who were there for Hajj would hear his recitation and adopt its non-Arabic mode of recitation." "Was that the express reason for what you did?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. When Hadhrat Miswar (RA) confirmed that it was, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "You did the right thing." [^2]
Hadhrat Talha (RA) asks a Congregation he had Led in salaah whether they were Pleased with his Salaah

Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) once led some people in salaah. When he turned to them (after completing the salaah), he said, "I had forgotten to consult with you before going ahead and leading the salaah. Are you pleased with my salaah?" "Of course," the congregation replied, "who will be displeased with it, O selected companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ." Hadhrat Talha (RA) then said, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that when a person leads others in salaah and they are displeased with him, the salaah does not even pass his ears (let alone reach the heavens)." [^3]
